issue.title: Migrate task-sdk from httpx to httpx2

repository.name: airflow
repository.description: Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows

issue.body:
## Summary

This PR migrates the task-sdk package from httpx to httpx2 as a proof-of-concept to test compatibility and identify any issues, as suggested by @potiuk in #70522.

It also updates the Airflow core in-process execution API to use the matching httpx2 sync and async transports.

### Background

The httpx library may not be actively maintained, and httpx2 (a fork of httpx 0.28.1) has been created with bug fixes and improvements. The maintainer of starlette has confirmed that starlette will migrate to httpx2, making the migration from httpx in FastAPI an eventuality.

### Approach

Following the httpx2 migration guide (https://httpx2.pydantic.dev/migration/), this PR uses direct httpx2 imports in the migrated code:

- Keeps httpx and httpx2 available together so packages that still depend on httpx are unaffected
- Allows incremental migration — each package or subpackage can be migrated independently
- Uses httpx2 transport implementations in the in-process execution API so client and transport types come from the same package

### Changes

- task-sdk/pyproject.toml: Changed the dependency from httpx>=0.27.0 to httpx2>=0.28.1
- task-sdk: Migrated API client, supervisor, tests, and model-generation imports from httpx to httpx2
- airflow-core/pyproject.toml: Added httpx2>=0.28.1 while retaining httpx for existing users
- airflow-core/src/airflow/api_fastapi/execution_api/app.py: Changed the in-process API to use httpx2.WSGITransport and httpx2.ASGITransport
- airflow-core/tests/unit/api_fastapi/execution_api/test_app.py: Added coverage for the httpx2 sync and async transports
- uv.lock: Updated dependency resolution for both packages

### Notes

- certifi usage in client.py is retained as-is — it is used directly for SSL context configuration, not through httpx, and is independent of the httpx/httpx2 choice
- The httpx2 package has the same public API as httpx 0.28.1, with direct imports used here rather than an alias
- Known behavior differences in httpx2: SSL verification uses the OS trust store via truststore instead of certifi bundled certificates, and the User-Agent header changes to python-httpx2/<version>

## Test plan

- [x] Focused task-sdk API client tests: 127 passed
- [x] Focused in-process execution API tests: 27 passed
- [x] Verify httpx2 installs cleanly alongside httpx: uv lock --check passed
- [x] Verify Client, MockTransport, and transport behavior through the focused tests
- [ ] Full task-sdk test suite
- [ ] CI checks pass

##### Was generative AI tooling used to co-author this PR?

- [X] Yes (Claude) following the guidelines (https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/contributing-docs/05_pull_requests.rst#gen-ai-assisted-contributions)

body:
I was curious to see if / how FastAPI was migrating to `httpx2`. Currently, it [looks like](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/16186) there might be some work towards a gradual migration. 

Given the split components of Airflow (core, sdk, providers), I think it might make sense to address each individually. My hunch is that this would be a good way to split out the migration:
* `airflow-core`: Temporarily support _both_ `httpx` and `httpx2`, with some tentative future release targetting the removal of `httpx`.
* `task-sdk`: It looks like this may be able to fully cutover in a single release.
* `airflow-providers`: Looking into this one currently, hoping to put up a PR for it if there aren't any unexpected issues.

## What?
* Modifies `apache-airflow-task-sdk`'s dependency on `httpx` → `httpx2`. The Execution API `Client` is now an `httpx2.Client`.

* Adds an [`ast-grep`](https://github.com/ast-grep/ast-grep) pre-commit check to prevent re-introducing `httpx` in the Task SDK, mirroring the providers one.

issue.title: Add async support in `apache-airflow-client`

repository.name: airflow
repository.description: Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows

issue.body:
### Description

Currently, the `apache-airflow-client` package (generated from the `openapi-generator-cli`) uses the default `urllib3` client, which does not support async operations.

The proposed feature is to generate and package `async` client code in the `apache-airflow-client` package, in addition to the existing synchronous client code. 
Ideally, this **should not** alter the synchronous interface to ensure this is not a breaking change.

### Use case/motivation

Async client usage is particularly helpful for users who either:
* Need to perform independent API operations in a single process (such as a bulk "pause dags" operation).
* Manage multiple Airflow instances, and require multi-plexing requests across instances (e.g. a management script which updates the same Airflow variables across multiple Airflow instances at once).
    * This is a situation I'm currently using async api calls for, but with httpx2 directly, rather than with the official Apache Airflow python client. It would be really nice to have the additional type safety the official client offers, and I'm sure this would benefit others as well.

As noted above, `urllib3` is the current client used in the client generation tool, but the upcoming release of `openapi-generator-cli` version `7.26.0` will support for generating code which uses `httpx2` under the hood. `httpx2` supports both sync and async operations. Additionally, the openapi-generator-cli has configuration options to generate code with both sync and async code in the same output package.

Both the `httpx2` and `async` code generation config options are described here: https://openapi-generator.tech/docs/generators/python/#config-options

### Related issues

Tangentially related: https://github.com/apache/airflow/issues/70522 
* context:`httpx` is apparently no longer actively maintained, and Pydantic's `httpx2` is the replacement that appears to have taken the designation as the python community's "accepted" replacement.

### Blocked Until

We can't implement this until the [`openapi-generator`](https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator) version `7.26.0` is released, since that is the first release which offers [`httpx2` support](https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/pull/24966).

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

- [x] Yes I am willing to submit a PR!

### Code of Conduct

- [x] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

issue.title: Fix Dag processor API client not catching Task SDK client errors

repository.name: airflow
repository.description: Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows

issue.body:
`DagProcessorAPIClient` (#74370) subclasses the Task SDK `Client`, which #73116 moved from `httpx` to `httpx2`. httpx2 has its own exception and transport classes, so the processor client's `except httpx.HTTPStatusError` / `httpx.HTTPError` / `httpx.ResponseNotRead` clauses stopped matching anything the client raises. Registration conflicts, closed-Job retirement and the early token-renewal fallbacks all fell through. On main, `dag_processing/test_api_client.py` and `execution_api/test_dag_processor_client.py` fail 86 of 98 tests, because `httpx.MockTransport` responses trip httpx2's `SyncByteStream` assertion.

- Move the processor client and its two test modules to `httpx2`. The test changes are the mechanical `httpx` → `httpx2` swap; no assertions changed.
- Let the Task SDK's `ServerResponseError.from_response` accept JSON errors whose `Content-Type` carries parameters (`application/json; charset=utf-8`) or different letter case. Those were raised as a bare `HTTPStatusError` with the body unread, so the processor client could not see the error `reason`.
- Ban `httpx` imports in airflow-core with ruff (`TID251`), as task-sdk already does, so the next mix-up is a lint error instead of failing tests. The six modules not yet migrated are exempt until #70522 moves them (wider migration also in #74244).

issue.title: [v3-4-test] Migrate Task SDK to `httpx2` (#73116)

repository.name: airflow
repository.description: Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows

issue.body:
* Depend on httpx2 instead of httpx in the Task SDK

httpx has stalled: fixes that landed in httpx2 (a fork of httpx 0.28.1)
have not shipped upstream, and starlette has already migrated, so FastAPI
following is a matter of time. Moving the Execution API client now keeps
the SDK on a maintained HTTP stack.

Objects do not cross the httpx/httpx2 boundary, so the in-process
Execution API transports move with the client that consumes them; the
rest of airflow-core stays on httpx and migrates separately.

related: https://github.com/apache/airflow/issues/70522

* Add newsfragment for the Task SDK httpx2 migration

* Match the in-process test client transport to the installed Task SDK

Compat tests pair the repo's devel-common helpers with a released Airflow
whose Task SDK is still on httpx. Pinning the helper to httpx2 hands those
clients a transport from the wrong package, and httpx rejects the response
stream it gets back.

* Rename newsfragment to the new PR number

* Pin the Task SDK ast-grep hook to a frozen revision

Every other third-party hook in the repo pins an immutable SHA; a mutable
tag lets the hook change under CI without a diff.

* Remove unneeded newsfragment

* Verify Task SDK HTTP logging and simplify test helpers

Both HTTP stacks can coexist while compatibility jobs use older SDK
distributions. The migration needs regression coverage for its logging
behavior without exposing development-only helpers as public APIs.

* Use httpx2 in the Dag run note client test

* Use httpx2 in the execution API shutdown tests

Tests added on main for in-process shutdown still referenced httpx, which this branch no longer imports in the module.

* Trust the system certificate store in the Task SDK API client

httpx2 verifies against the system trust store via truststore, so keeping certifi for the Execution API client would add a direct dependency only to maintain a second, different set of trusted roots in the same worker.

* Ban httpx imports in the Task SDK with ruff

Ruff already enforces banned imports, so a separate ast-grep hook and its extra pre-commit dependency are unnecessary. extend-banned-api adds to the root banned-api table instead of replacing it.

* Use httpx2 in the server termination acknowledgement test

The test arrived on main after the Task SDK moved to httpx2 and still referenced httpx, which the module no longer imports.

* Test the Task SDK SSL context against a real CA file

Mocking load_verify_locations while also writing a CA file to disk tested neither path convincingly. Keeping the certificate-generation imports inside the fixture limits them to the one place that needs them.

* Note when the in-process httpx resolver can be removed

* Apply suggestion from @ashb

Co-authored-by: Ash Berlin-Taylor <ash_github@firemirror.com>

* Use httpx2 in the supervisor launch error test helper

The helper arrived on main after the Task SDK moved to httpx2 and still referenced httpx, which the module no longer imports.

* Remove the duplicated in-process httpx resolver note

* Use httpx2 in the supervisor execution timeout test

The test arrived on main after the Task SDK moved to httpx2 and still referenced httpx, which the module no longer imports.

* Use httpx2 in the request handler tests

The tests arrived on main after the Task SDK moved to httpx2; the client rejects httpx transports.

---------

Co-authored-by: Zach <zach.gottesman@datadoghq.com>
Co-authored-by: Ash Berlin-Taylor <ash_github@firemirror.com>
